messages:
kai: Pushed a quick KV cache microbench across regions/GPU types. Focus was on bursty short-sequence traffic and how eviction interacts with streaming refcounts. summary + config below, looking for quick eyeballs before I bake this into the runbook.

kai: ```
# aggregated summary (short, balanced, long mixes)
Region | GPU    | seq-mix      | hit% | p50(ms) | p99(ms) | tps
US     | H100   | short-heavy  | 82   | 12      | 98      | 420
EU     | A100   | balanced     | 74   | 18      | 210     | 310
APAC   | H100   | long-heavy   | 65   | 30      | 450     | 160
US     | H100q  | short-heavy  | 78   | 10      | 120     | 460
```

kai: Notes: APAC H100 run shows p99 blowup under sustained bursts -- trace points to many entries marked in-use (ref_count) and not eligible for eviction, causing the pager to churn and kernel switch thrash.

maya: Interesting. Did you use staged eviction or immediate purge? Also what's your prefetch window?

kai: ```
# run config
prefetch.window=32
evict.mode=soft+staged   # try soft reclaim first, then hard after delay
evict.threshold=0.6      # trigger when cache usage > 60%
ttl.prune.interval=0      # off for first sweep (to reproduce ghosting)
spill.fallback=cpu_async
kernel.policy=auto_quant_select
```

ron: APAC p99=450 is worrying. Is the kernel selector bouncing between fp16 and int8 under pressure? That can add 50-200ms depending on cache hits.

kai: Yep, kernel logs show frequent kernel-switch events when eviction > 3 ops/sec per GPU. The switch penalty + page IO is what amplifies p99.

dina: @kai did you look for 'ghost entries' where streaming sessions keep refcounts nonzero (e.g., tool calls with streaming tokens)? We saw similar last quarter. TTL prune sweep every 2s helped then.

kai: Good call. I re-ran with ttl.prune.interval=2 and a short TTL for ephemeral sessions, plus an active sweep job that forces staged->hard after 1.5s. Results: p99 cut ~2x in APAC.

kai: ```
# before/after (APAC H100, long-heavy)
metric | before | after
p99   | 450    | 220
hit%  | 65     | 68
tps   | 160    | 190
```

maya: Nice improvement. Did quantized kernel keep the same behaviour?

kai: For short-heavy mixes H100q still had advantage on throughput, but quantized kernel's smaller working set slightly increases eviction churn in some traces. We reduced churn by increasing prefetch.window -> 48 for H100q.

ron: How about capacity sizing? Any guidance from these runs for Reserved pools?

kai: Quick rules of thumb from the bench:
- For short-heavy traffic, size for target tps at p99 with hit% ~80% to allow batching headroom.
- For mixed/long, plan +25% headroom or route long seqs to dedicated long-worker pool.
- Enable ttl-prune sweep on all regions; it stabilizes p99 across load spikes.

dina: Also flagging: add a metric for kernel-switch rate and page-evict/sec to console dashboards. Those two correlate strongly with p99 spikes.

kai: Filed a tiny runbook PR with configs and the 'force-sweep' mitigation. Will add dashboards next.
